problem: Each share is rounded independently with ROUND_HALF_UP after an inexact, context-dependent Decimal division and leftover units are never redistributed, so the shares no longer sum to amount ("100",[1,1,1] -> 99.99; "0.05",[1,1] -> 0.06), creating or losing money.
_ref.allocate on line 18 consumes a generator/iterator passed as weights, so line 20 builds an empty list and the function silently returns [] for a valid request.

Values are validated by _ref.allocate but recomputed from a second read via Decimal(str(x)), so an int/str subclass overriding __str__ or an iterable yielding different values on re-iteration bypasses validation (EvilInt(10) is paid out as 1000000; negative or NaN shares possible).
The full reference allocation is run only for its exceptions and its correct result is discarded, doubling the work and making the production path depend on reference_impl.
The behavioral rewrite ships with no test of the sum-equals-amount invariant, one-shot iterables, or rounding, any of which would have caught F1 and F2.
Fraction is imported but no longer used (ruff F401).
Decimal is imported a second time, redefining the line-1 import (ruff F811).
_to_decimal is now dead code, which misleadingly suggests it still guards the allocation path.
Validation for the money path now hinges on a top-level import of reference_impl, which any same-named module earlier on sys.path would silently replace.
